pr.title: Be a bit more careful around exotic cycles in in the inliner
pr.author: compiler-errors

analysis.summary: The MIR inliner's cycle query (`mir_callgraph_cyclic` in `inline/cycle.rs`) used an `FxHashSet` named `seen` to avoid revisiting instances. That lost the information that an already-visited callee reaches the root, so when a recursive callee was reachable through more than one path, the second path was skipped and the local caller was never added to `involved` as recursive. Two mutually recursive functions could therefore each fail to consider the other a recursion participant, producing a query cycle. Fix: `seen` becomes `FxHashMap<Instance, bool>` caching "reaches root"; direct target hits are inserted as `true`, cached values are propagated on revisits, and `involved` is populated whenever a callee reaches the root.
analysis.originalLogic: In `process`, `seen: &mut FxHashSet<ty::Instance>` tracks instances already visited. For each resolved callee: if `callee.def_id() == target.to_def_id()`, set `cycle_found = true` (but do not record the target in `seen`). Otherwise, after skipping constructors/non-inlined callees, `if seen.insert(callee) { ... recurse ... if found_recursion { involved.insert(local def); cycle_found = true; } }`. A callee already present in `seen` is skipped entirely, so no information about whether it reaches the root is propagated to the current caller. The function returns `cycle_found`. `mir_callgraph_cyclic` initializes with `&mut FxHashSet::default()`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect behavior is the early-out `if seen.insert(callee)` combined with a set: when `seen.insert(callee)` returns `false` (callee already visited), the loop skips the callee and does not mark the current caller as reaching the root, even if that callee is on a path back to the root. The direct target match also does not record the target instance in `seen`. Consequently, a callee that reaches the root via cycle A but has already been visited while exploring cycle B is treated as if it did not reach the root on the B path; the enclosing local function is never inserted into `involved`, so mutually recursive functions can each omit the other as a recursion participant, leading to a query cycle. The corrected transformation replaces the set with a map from instance to "reaches root", records `true` on direct target match, and on a revisit propagates the cached boolean instead of dropping it.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR/optimization input for the `Inline` pass: functions compiled with `-Zinline-mir`, especially mutually recursive `#[inline]` functions that call each other through function-item `FnOnce::call_once` (requiring `#![feature(fn_traits)]` and edition 2021). The cycle graph must contain a callee reachable by multiple paths where a foreign item (e.g. the `FnOnce::call_once` shim) lies on the cycle, and at least one function has multiple call terminators. The regression test uses `EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`, `test-mir-pass: Inline`, `-Zinline-mir --crate-type=lib`, emitting `inline_double_cycle.a.Inline.diff` and `inline_double_cycle.b.Inline.diff` under both panic-abort and panic-unwind. More generally, the domain is any DFS cycle reachability query where the same cyclic node can be reached through more than one branch (diamond/multiple-cycle graphs), not only the concrete fn_traits example.
analysis.trigger: A recursive callee is encountered more than once during the cycle DFS: the first visit recurses (possibly discovering that it reaches the root), but the second visit sees the instance already in `seen` and is skipped. If the second occurrence is the one that would have propagated "reaches root" to the current caller, that caller is not added to `involved`. In the fn_traits example, `<{a} as FnOnce>::call_once` recurses into `a` (a cyclical path through a foreign item not marked as a cyclic def id), then `<{b} as FnOnce>::call_once` recurses into `b`; when `b` calls `<{a} as FnOnce>::call_once`, `a` is already in `seen`, so the recursion is not propagated, `b` is not collected as recursive, and similarly in the flipped direction this yields two functions that do not consider each other recursive, causing a query cycle.
preconditions: The inliner's cyclic-callgraph query is running (`mir_callgraph_cyclic` / `process`) as part of the Inline pass.
At least two local functions participate in a mutually recursive call graph.
A cycle passes through a non-local/foreign item such as the `FnOnce::call_once` shim, which is not recorded as a cyclical def id.
A recursive instance is reachable through multiple call paths, so the same instance appears again after already being inserted into `seen`.
The function has multiple call terminators, allowing one branch to revisit an instance first seen on another branch.
pitfalls: Treating `seen` as a plain set only answers 'have we visited this instance', not 'does this instance reach the root'; memoized reachability must be stored per instance.
Directly matching the target (`callee.def_id() == target.to_def_id()`) must record that callee as reaching the root; otherwise later revisits cannot propagate it.

Non-local def ids (foreign items such as `FnOnce::call_once`) cannot be added to `involved` because calling `optimized_mir` on them cannot cycle, but their cycle participation still must be propagated.
Recursion-limit exhaustion pessimistically returns true; this interacts with the cached boolean and should not be confused with a confirmed cycle.

Test diff changes showing `call_once` shims being inlined are the corrected output, not evidence that a replacement pass is wrong; the historical bug was missing recursion detection, not a bad inline rewrite.
DFS traversal order must not determine whether a mutually recursive function is recognized; both directions (`a` and `b` roots) need coverage.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a `tests/mir-opt` regression test with two mutually recursive `#[inline]` functions using `FnOnce::call_once` on their own function-item types. Use `// EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`, `//@ test-mir-pass: Inline`, `//@ edition: 2021`, `//@ compile-flags: -Zinline-mir --crate-type=lib`, and emit both `a` and `b` Inline MIR diffs. This exercises the cycle query from both roots and both panic strategies. The expected corrected MIR shows the `call_once` shims inlined into calls through temporary function pointers (e.g. `_1 = move _5()` with `scope 1 (inlined <fn() {a} as FnOnce<()>>::call_once - shim(fn() {a}))`), rather than the pre-inline `_1 = <fn() {a} as FnOnce<()>>::call_once(a, move _2)`. To isolate the transformation, compare an implementation that caches root-reachability per visited instance against one that only stores a set and drops revisits; keep the same mutually recursive program and assert that both functions are recognized as recursive / no query cycle occurs. Note: no compiler was built here, so this is a testing design, not a reproduction claim.
